subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 8
syllabus: Victorian Curriculum F-10 Version 2.0: Mathematics, Level 8

points.title: Rational and irrational numbers
points.brief: A rational number can be written as a fraction of two integers. An irrational number, such as pi or √2, cannot, and its decimal never ends or repeats.

points.title: Index laws for multiplying and dividing
points.brief: With the same base, add the indices to multiply and subtract them to divide, such as 2⁵ × 2³ = 2⁸ and 2⁵ ÷ 2³ = 2².

points.title: Power of a power and the zero index
points.brief: Raising a power to a power multiplies the indices, such as (3²)⁴ = 3⁸, and any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1.

points.title: Terminating and recurring decimals
points.brief: Divide the numerator by the denominator to turn a fraction into a decimal that either ends or repeats, and write repeating digits with a dot or bar.

points.title: Multiplying and dividing integers
points.brief: Two numbers with the same sign give a positive answer, and different signs give a negative one, such as -4 × -3 = 12.

points.title: Percentage increase and decrease
points.brief: Multiply by a single factor, such as 1.15 for a 15% increase or 0.8 for a 20% discount.

points.title: Finding a percentage change
points.brief: Divide the change by the original amount and multiply by 100, such as a rise from $40 to $50 being a 25% increase.

points.title: Percentage error
points.brief: The difference between an estimate and the true value, as a percentage of the true value.

points.title: Profit and loss
points.brief: Profit is selling price minus cost price, a loss when negative, and it can be written as a percentage of the cost price.

points.title: Simplifying with like terms
points.brief: Like terms have the same variables to the same powers, so 5x + 3y - 2x simplifies to 3x + 3y.

points.title: Expanding brackets
points.brief: Multiply each term inside by the term outside, taking care with negatives, such as -2(x - 4) = -2x + 8.

points.title: Factorising with a common factor
points.brief: Take out the highest common factor of every term and put the rest in brackets, such as 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).

points.title: Equations with brackets and unknowns on both sides
points.brief: Expand any brackets, collect the unknowns on one side and the numbers on the other, then solve and check by substituting.

points.title: Graphing straight lines from a table
points.brief: Make a table of values from a rule such as y = 3x - 2, plot the points and join them with a straight line.

points.title: Solving equations with a graph
points.brief: Read the x value where a line reaches a given y value, or where two lines cross, to solve an equation.

points.title: Inequality signs and number lines
points.brief: What <, >, ≤ and ≥ mean, and showing a solution such as x > 3 on a number line with an open or closed circle.

points.title: Linear models with a fixed cost
points.brief: A cost made of a fixed charge plus a rate, such as C = 20 + 5h, and using the rule or its graph to find costs and the break-even point.

points.title: Composite shapes
points.brief: Find the area of an irregular shape by splitting it into rectangles and triangles, or by subtracting a cut-out part, and find its perimeter by adding the outside edges.

points.title: Volume and capacity
points.brief: Capacity is how much a container holds. 1 cm³ holds 1 mL and 1 m³ holds 1000 L, so a prism's volume gives its capacity.

points.title: Circumference of a circle
points.brief: The circumference is pi times the diameter, or 2 times pi times the radius.

points.title: Area of a circle
points.brief: The area is pi times the radius squared, so halve the diameter first, and give the answer in square units.

points.title: Time zones and 24-hour time
points.brief: Converting between 12-hour and 24-hour time, working out durations, and adding or subtracting hours across time zones.

points.title: Rates and unit rates
points.brief: A rate compares quantities with different units, such as 120 km in 2 hours. A unit rate gives the amount for one unit, 60 km/h.

points.title: Speed, distance and time
points.brief: Speed is distance divided by time, so distance is speed times time and time is distance divided by speed, with matching units.

points.title: Pythagoras' theorem for the hypotenuse
points.brief: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, so c = √(a² + b²).

points.title: Finding a shorter side with Pythagoras
points.brief: To find a shorter side, subtract the square of the known short side from the square of the hypotenuse, then take the square root.

points.title: Congruent figures
points.brief: Congruent figures are the same shape and size, so matching sides and angles are equal, even if one is flipped or turned.

points.title: Tests for congruent triangles
points.brief: Two triangles are congruent if they match by SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS. Two sides and a non-included angle is not enough.

points.title: Similar figures and scale factor
points.brief: Similar figures have equal angles and sides in the same ratio. The scale factor is a new length divided by the matching old length.

points.title: Proving properties of quadrilaterals
points.brief: Drawing a diagonal makes congruent triangles, which show facts such as a parallelogram's opposite sides being equal and its diagonals bisecting each other.

points.title: Three-dimensional coordinates
points.brief: A point in space is given by (x, y, z), adding a third axis for height to the usual x and y.

points.title: Population and sample
points.brief: The population is the whole group being studied. A sample is part of it, used when asking everyone is too costly or slow.

points.title: Census, survey, experiment and observation
points.brief: The ways to collect data, from a census of everyone to a sample survey, a controlled experiment or watching and recording.

points.title: Random and biased samples
points.brief: In a random sample every member has an equal chance of being picked. A sample of volunteers or friends can be biased.

points.title: Sample size and variation
points.brief: Different random samples from the same population give different results, and larger samples vary less from each other.

points.title: Complementary events
points.brief: An event and its complement cover every outcome, so their probabilities add to 1 and P(not A) = 1 - P(A).

points.title: Two-way tables for two events
points.brief: A two-way table sorts outcomes by two features at once, and the counts give probabilities such as P(boy and plays sport).

points.title: Venn diagrams and probability
points.brief: Overlapping circles show "A and B" in the overlap and "A or B" as everything in either circle, which gives their probabilities.

points.title: Tree diagrams for two steps
points.brief: A tree diagram lists every outcome of two events, such as tossing a coin twice, so each combined outcome's probability can be counted.
